beats.text: Welcome to episode nine. Last time we assumed that all the useful heat went into the water. In a real calorimeter, that isn't quite true, and today we'll fix it with a technique called calibration.
A quick check first. How much energy warms one hundred and twenty point zero grams of water by four point zero zero degrees? Pause and calculate.

Using q equals m c delta T: one hundred and twenty point zero times four point one eight times four point zero zero, which is two thousand and six point four joules. Keep that number in mind; it's close to, but not the same as, what a real calorimeter needs.
